name: Stoddard Buttress

pitch_detail.notes: Scrambling to gain the buttress crest, left of the 1961 line
Long stretches of low-fifth simul-climbing along the crest
Two exposed knife-edge pitches and a sharp prow near the top; the route's 5.8 crux

rappel_detail.notes: First rappel off the ridge crest working down toward the notch by the large chockstone that marks the top of the descent gully.
rappel_detail.anchor: Slung horn/chockstone near West Ridge crest

rappel_detail.notes: Second rappel finishing the ridge-crest section; some parties do only one here and downclimb/simul-downclimb the rest.
First rappel down the loose, rockfall-prone gully into Crescent Creek Basin; a single 50-60m rope is sufficient for every reported station.
rappel_detail.anchor: Natural chockstone/horn anchor in the descent gully

rappel_detail.notes: Final gully rappel; the last ~100 ft below this is loose and marginal and is downclimbed.

rappels: About 4 rappels on a single 60 m rope down the West Ridge descent: one or two near the ridge crest above the notch, then two or three in the loose gully to Crescent Creek Basin; three to five depending on snow and how much is downclimbed
descent_text: Rappel/scramble the West Ridge to the Blob (The Rake)-Terror notch (2 rappels of ~30m), then descend a chossy, steep-snow gully with several rappels, one of them past an overhanging chockstone, back into Crescent Creek Cirque. On the original ascent the return proved unexpectedly difficult, including a six-hour bushwhack after a barrier crossing went wrong.
approach: Same as the North Buttress: from the Goodell Creek trailhead follow the old roadbed trail and a climbers' path to Terror Creek at about 2,000 ft, cross it, and climb the very steep path up the Barrier, the ridge beyond. Follow its crest north into Stump Hollow, make a rising traverse to the 6,400 ft saddle northeast of The Chopping Block, and downclimb about 200 ft into Crescent Creek Basin to the high camp (~6,000 ft gain, ~7-7.5 hrs), then on the climbing day cross the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and descend the Mustard Glacier to the base of the north face (2-3 hrs from camp). Stoddard's original approach used a two-day approach via Stettattle Ridge and the upper McMillan Creek cirque.
overview: A left-trending, more aesthetic variation of the original 1961 North Buttress, climbing long stretches of low-fifth to 5.8 rock up the buttress crest between McMillan Cirque and the summit, finishing across two exposed knife-edge pitches.
beta: Widely regarded as the most inspiring line on Terror's north side: Stoddard traversed left of the 1961 route to gain a cleaner crest, following solid rock through a narrow face between two buttresses and a long, spectacular arete section to the summit area.
fa: John Stoddard, solo, July 16, 1984 (IV 5.8); an extended/left-side finish variant was climbed by Stoddard July 14-17, 1985 and is known as "North Face, Left Side" (5.8+)
face: North Face, left (east) rib, above McMillan Cirque
